purpose: Follow the exposed destination-only timing audit. Measure a conditional continuous-meal bound under unchanged shipments and worker calendars. This is development, not a blind Earth test or a revised population estimate.
cohort: All eight coherent provider-year scenarios; every already calendar-qualified provider retained. Two pulse calendars B (original destination-bin starts) and C (selected collector return phases), giving 16 complete scenario rows. All 18 actor summaries and every scored provider retained. Unqualified providers remain explicitly unscored.
fixed_inputs: Use the reviewed delivery-timing events, original one-bin lag, 0.95 transport retention already applied once, original source shipments, original 5% stored-food loss, 365-day year and 2500 kcal/person/day. Physical storage capacity stays the ORIGINAL 90-day-of-parent-total-demand amount, even when trial meals decrease. Source food assumptions and all selected worker jobs remain unchanged. Do not invent grain, reassign providers, reduce workers, remove staff meals, change policies or edit map packets/defaults.
meal_trial: Keep all original institutional residents and their meals fixed. Multiply only the original civilian resident meal count by alpha in [0,1], independently per provider. Total trial daily demand is 2500*(original institutional residents + alpha*original civilian residents). Verify these components sum to the parent total exactly within source precision; no staff double count. Alpha is a demand accounting parameter, not relocation, mortality, a census or food/work recoupling.
solver: First score alpha=0 and alpha=1. If staff-only meals fail, retain an explicit infeasible_staff_meals flag, no feasible civilian alpha and no fictitious supported population. If alpha=1 passes, keep 1. Otherwise bracket the largest passing alpha with 48 deterministic bisections on [0,1]. Use the SAME original diagnostic unmet <= 1e-8*max(1,annual needed kcal), with a separate continuous unmet amount. Retain both final passing and failing bounds, residual interval width, all endpoint fields and monotonicity checks. Find the smallest periodic nonnegative inventory for each trial; never inject inherited reserve.
outputs: All 16 rows, every scored provider and actor: unchanged staff/civilian/parent residents, passing and failing alpha bounds, conditional meal-equivalent civilian reduction, parent/full-demand gap, staff-only feasibility, periodic initial/final/peak stock, consumed/unmet/spoilage/overflow, shortfall duration and food/periodic residuals at the selected passing bound. Show B versus C without choosing a best policy. Do not map these conditional meal equivalents as new population estimates.
controls_and_review: Before production, test fixed-staff preservation, original-capacity preservation, staff-only failure, full-demand pass, tight intermediate bound, no external reserve, deterministic brackets, monotone unmet and input nonmutation. Reuse continuous-inventory manufactured controls. Independent scalar integration and separate bracket search must check every final passing/failing bound, original source identities and exact fixed inputs. Fresh fields/results/provider CSV byte exact. All rows and figures in normal research, all figures posted, browser/mobile/Windows checks and old atlas byte preservation.
limits: Destination cereal inventory only. Lower destination meal demand is not a valid final population reallocation because civilian field work, source exports and other resource needs remain frozen. Full resident reoptimization must recompute the shared source/food/work ledger, integer shipments and worker calendars. Source within-bin availability, crew-carried food and food location, complete diets and household/draft work, actual provider roles, dated occupancy and size evidence, prospective transfer, mobile/nonstate/unaffiliated integration remain open.
continuation: Review the entire release 1–4 / S1–S5 programme, push the completed checkpoint and CONTINUE. No calibrated adoption or default update.
